title: Chicago jazz bands: Erskine Tate and Dave Payton
summary: Amacker describes Chicago jazz in the early years and the bands of Erskine Tate at the Vendome and Dave Payton.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well they had regular jazz music then. It was a jazz world and it was really a jazz music. The rest of the people copied from those bands then, you know, they picked it up from those bands. And so they had all the fellas, this is Dave, this is Oiskin Tate, was a very famous band playing at that time. You heard talk of him?
Sure. Did you? Teddy Weatherford? What? What I was saying. Wonderful piano player. I got a record by them, with Louis on the cornet.

Dave Payton, you heard Dave Payton. Joe Oliver used to play with him after Joe broke up his band. You heard of him in front of them. What the shit you said? Dave Payton and Oiskin Tate, he was director at the Vendome Theatre.
He's teaching music now. I guess he gave up playing the violin.
He was a nice violinist. Nice violinist and he played at the Vendome Theatre. Dave Payton was a crackerjack. In those days he was a cracker.
